A class with only `static` members has nothing to instantiate. It groups values and functions under a name, and a plain object does that with less syntax.

A class is not reported if it extends another class, has a decorator, is empty, or has a member that an object cannot have: a private `#name`, a static block, or in TypeScript a member marked `readonly`, `declare`, `public`, `protected` or `private`.

`--fix-dangerously` rewrites the class to an object. `--fix` does not, because code that calls `new` on the class or uses it as a type stops working.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
class Temperature {
  static freezing = 32;

  static toCelsius(fahrenheit) {
    return ((fahrenheit - 32) * 5) / 9;
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const Temperature = {
  freezing: 32,

  toCelsius(fahrenheit) {
    return ((fahrenheit - 32) * 5) / 9;
  },
};
```

A private member keeps the class:

{/* good */}
```js
class Counter {
  static #count = 0;

  static next() {
    return ++Counter.#count;
  }
}
```

So does a TypeScript modifier:

{/* good */}
```ts
class Limits {
  static readonly maxRetries = 3;
  private static attempts = 0;
}
```
